chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Al-A'ala ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:
I said to him (peace be upon him): 'From where should I touch the Kaaba when I have finished my Tawaf?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'From its back.'

key_terms.الْكَعْبَة: The Kaaba, the cubic building in Mecca

ai.seo_question: Where should a pilgrim touch the Kaaba after finishing Tawaf?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the Multazam as the specific locus for Istilam after Tawaf, a practice rooted in the tradition of the Ahl al-Bayt. Scholarly consensus identifies this spot between the door and the Black Stone as the place where Prophet Ibrahim (AS) stood while supplicating for his son Ismail, thereby linking the ritual to prophetic lineage and divine acceptance. The instruction underscores the significance of physical proximity to the Kaaba's structural anchors during the final stages of circumambulation.
